title: installer: add artifact rotation + rollforward metadata pipeline for private-installer
author: Liam O'Connor
description:
Motivation: private-installer releases were accumulating redundant artifacts and lacked machine-readable 'rollforward' metadata for fast upgrades in air-gapped installs. This PR introduces a pipeline and small runtime pieces to: 1) rotate old release artifacts (TTL-based, retention policy per-channel), 2) produce a compact rollforward manifest that describes upgrade-compatible artifact sequences, 3) integrate Helm chart checksum validation into release index generation, and 4) pin Terraform module references and embed provenance attestations so private customers can verify end-to-end integrity.

What this change does (high-level):
- New CI pipeline job 'installer-release-rotate' that runs nightly and performs TTL-based pruning of artifacts stored in release-bucket and artifact-catalog; supports dry-run and --apply modes.
- 'rollforward.json' manifest generator added to release indexer. Manifest includes ordered artifact IDs, required minimal delta patch, target helm checksums, and recommended rollback anchor.
- Integrates cosign signing step into the rotate pipeline for newly generated rollforward manifests and for Helm chart tarballs. Attestations (in-tree predicate) emitted to provenance/ folder.
- Adds a verifier CLI subcommand rw-release verify --manifest which validates signatures, compares Helm chart checksums, and checks SBOM hashes. This runs as part of e2e-installer job.
- Terraform module pinning: release pipeline now produces a terraform-modules.lock file with module source@version entries for the installer terraform modules to make upgrades deterministic.
- Fix: previous rollback implementation sometimes referenced stale index shards; the indexer rewrite ensures each shard has a canonical manifest and adds deterministic shard checksums to the ledger.

Checklist: - [x] Pipeline job added to CI config with toggle flags and required secrets. - [x] Indexer change tested locally against a synthetic bucket. - [x] cosign integration wired and documented. - [x] rw-release verify implemented and exercised in CI. - [x] Backwards-compatible: existing release indexes remain queryable; new rollforward manifests are optional for older installers.

Why this is safe: rotation runs in dry-run by default and requires a release engineer toggle to apply; signing steps reuse existing cosign keys and stick to current KMS practices. Rollforward manifests are additive; agents still can use old index flow.

Related: MAY help prevent incidents similar to SUP-122 that required manual artifact pruning and manual manifest stitching. See linked Linear ENG-4321 for rollforward format design notes.

review_conversation: Aisha Patel: Please add a short migration note for existing customers. How will older installers behave when rollforward.json exists?

Author (Liam): Added docs/private-installer/release-notes/rollforward.md explaining that rollforward is optional; installers older than 2024-11 will ignore it. Added a compatibility test in e2e-suite.
Miguel Ortega: The default rotation retention looks aggressive for enterprise customers; can we make the retention per-channel configurable from the console?
Author (Liam): Retention is now a pipeline variable and we added a channel-to-retention mapping in CI. Also documented the required RBAC to flip the apply toggle.
Dana Kim: Ran the e2e flow and cosign verification passed; one remaining nit: make the verifier exit code 2 for 'inconclusive' so that ops tooling can differentiate.
Author (Liam): Updated rw-release verify to return code 2 on inconclusive checks and added unit tests.
notes_for_release: Additive: introduces rollforward.json in release indexes; optional for older installers.
New pipeline job 'installer-release-rotate' (nightly) with dry-run default; ops toggle required to apply.
rw-release verify: CLI helper to validate manifests, chart checksums, and signatures. Useful for air-gapped install verification.
security_considerations: Cosign keys reused from current release pipeline; new attestation predicate reviewed by security team.
Rotation requires vault-stored toggle; CI will fail fast if toggle secret is missing to avoid accidental deletion.
how_to_test: 1) Run hack/simulate_release_bucket.sh to create a synthetic bucket with multiple channel artifacts.
2) Run ci/pipelines/installer-release-rotate.yml in dry-run mode: ./scripts/ci-run.sh installer-release-rotate --dry-run
3) Generate rollforward with tools/indexer/rollforward_generator locally and inspect rollforward.json for expected sequence.
4) Use rw-release verify --manifest rollforward.json to validate signatures and chart checksums.
5) Toggle apply in CI with appropriate secrets to run a real prune; validate ledger consistency with hashchain-check.
